FRIDAY MORNING WEATHER
(Powered By: Rose City Air & Altra Federal Credit Union) 

Good morning and welcome to Friday. It looks and feels more like late-May as opposed to late-April out there this morning. Temps are at or slightly above the 70° mark in most places as we start the day.
• The warmer temp usually means moist air as well, and that’s a good way to describe what we’re working with across the area this morning with dew points in the mid to high 60s. 
• With the added moisture to the mix, we will obviously be a bit more on the humid side today compared to even yesterday, especially when you consider the fact that we’ll likely be a few degrees warmer today than we were yesterday. 
• I also think we’ll at least have a few showers dot the radar today, although most folks will stay dry. Still, the chance is there and I don’t want to catch anyone off guard. That said, the more organized potential for showers and thunderstorms will occur this evening & into the overnight as better lift arrives and storms erupt to our north over Oklahoma and try to ride toward the southeast across Northeast Texas. 
• In light of the potential for stronger storms to develop in this environment, SPC has expanded its “Slight” risk outline to cover most of East Texas, specifically for tonight. More recent short-term models are barking about better coverage of storms and an environment to support ‘em. Also, coverage has consistently looked better across the eastern half of the area during that same window of time. 
• All modes of severe weather will be on the table for tonight, and this is something that will get more attention as we go through the day and afternoon. 
• As far as the weekend itself is concerned, while we will carry the mention of low-end severe weather potential as far south as I-20, the chances for seeing any rain at all through that period in places like Tyler and Longview are pretty low. Most of what comes down will do so over the northern & eastern-most counties as storms continue to fire up in Oklahoma both late-tomorrow and again likely on Sunday afternoon before tracking southeast. This will ultimately put a pretty tight gradient of rainfall totals in place through the weekend with those north and east faring much better than their neighbors to the south and west in general.
• A somewhat better potential for some showers and thunderstorms areawide will return to the area as we get into the new work week as the pattern flexes even more. Temps will also try to ease somewhat as a result.
• FYI: I am scheduled to have an oral surgical procedure done later today. This will likely render me unable to talk through the weekend, and that’s not something that was even on my radar until day before yesterday. That said, my normal coverage for any significant severe weather will be affected due to this. I just wanted to keep you in the loop.   

☀️ Today • Sunrise: 6:46 am - Sunset: 7:54 pm | Total Daylight: 13:08 (+1:50) ⎥ Tyler Normals: 55/77 – Records: 91°/2011 -- 36°/1982  – 4.29”/1966

📊 Lower 48 Temp Extremes for Thursday:  102° at Rio Grande Village 🔹 11° at 22 miles southwest of Manila, Utah

• Thursday Climate Stats • Tyler City: 67/82 (0) -- Tyler Pounds: 67/82 (0) -- Longview: 68/83 (0) – Lufkin: 68/85 (0) #etxwx #txwx

Car rallies and gatherings may cause intermittent traffic slowdowns.

Commuters are advised to avoid the Muneerabad route during peak hours and use alternative routes.
 
Entry of heavy vehicles into Muneerabad village roads is strictly prohibited.

Heavy vehicles will be diverted via #Kandlakoya service road / #ORR service roads.

#CMRCollege X Road :

- #Traffic towards Muneerabad village will be diverted via:
#Kandlakoya ORR Service Road towards shamirpet ORR.

Plan  your travel in advance and avoid the affected routes .

Use alternate routes to reach #Medchal, #Kistapur, and surrounding areas. 

@cyberabadpolice
